inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K statement of changes in equity: 'Movement in share-based payments reserve' -18 (net reversal); LTI plan is equity-settled but immaterial and net negative in both FY25 (-165) and FY26 (-18) -- treated as an SBC-zero market per section 7(e)
inputs.share_count_basis: 24,591,464 fully paid ordinary shares on issue at 31 March 2026 (FY2026 10-K balance sheet note and shareholder register), POST the 40-for-1 share consolidation effective 6-Mar-2026 and POST the Sept-2025 rights issue + Amari placement. Basic = diluted per the FY2026 EPS note (potential ordinary shares antidilutive given the loss). Held FLAT: no material SBC to charge and no other dilutive instruments in the money.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, modelled as a flat 3.9% of revenue anchored to FY2026's $8,042k principal / $208,163k revenue = 3.86%) is deducted inside the flow build (see projections row 'lease'), and lease liabilities ($69,532k at FY2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. net_debt = interest-bearing liabilities only ($35,241k) less cash ($8,266k) = $26,975k, which ties to the company's own disclosed 'Net debt at 31 March' figure of $26,975k -- confirming this is the treatment the company itself effectively uses in its covenant/net-debt reporting.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-denominated flows discounted at a NZD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.5% (NZ 10yr govt, mid-2026), ERP 5.5%, beta 1.15 (cyclical building-materials processor) => unlevered CoE proxy ~10.8%. A +3.0pp small-cap/illiquidity/control premium is stacked on top (base WACC 13.5%) for: (i) micro-cap NZX/ASX dual-listed stock with market cap ~NZ$23m and thin free float (2,205 NZX holders, largest non-Amari holder <0.3%), (ii) 51% single-shareholder control (Amari/MGI) via board representation, (iii) only ~11 months since the Sept-2025 recapitalisation removed going-concern doubt -- covenant headroom is still unproven through a full cycle. This mirrors the stacked-WACC treatment applied to comparable NZX micro-caps in this folder (2CC.NZ 19%, CDI.NZ / AGL.NZ 17%). Per section 7(f), construction-cycle risk itself is charged in the flows via the probability-weighted scenarios, NOT via a further WACC premium or per-scenario WACC spread beyond the small bear/bull adjustment used to reflect distinct capital-structure/solvency risk in the bear case (15.0%) versus a lower-risk bull case (12.5%) -- this spread reflects solvency-tail risk in the bear case specifically (covenant stress), not cyclicality generally, which lives in the bear case's lower growth/margin path.
inputs.model: Owner-FCF DCF (operating company, non-US/cyclical adaptations per dcf-methods skill section 7)
inputs.notes: MPG.NZ is an operating industrial company (glass processing/glazing for NZ+AU construction) -- routes to the owner-FCF DCF engine, NOT a REIT/bank/LIC model. Section 7 adaptations applied: (a) NZD-built WACC (above); (b) lease treatment B (leases as opex, above); (c) no NCI (MPG has no material minority interests in its subsidiaries); (d) no material non-operating investment assets to strip income from; (e) SBC-zero market -- SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position set to null; (f) cyclicality charged once, in the probability-weighted scenario flows, not stacked into WACC on top of the control/liquidity premium. 10-year explicit horizon used because year-5 owner-FCF margin (5.6% base case) is still materially below the modelled mature level and the business is only 1-2 years off a cyclical trough -- a 5-year Gordon capitalization would freeze an immature margin. historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (equity CAGR rejected as the primary driver -- see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.8% to -7.4%) and revenue CAGR (-2.2% to -7.6%) both negative but NEITHER is usable as a forward growth proxy without adjustment. FY2026 shareholders' equity ($59,958k) was inflated by the Sept-2025 $23.9m dilutive capital raise, not organic compounding -- ex-raise equity would have kept falling toward the FY2025 trough ($35,582k). EPS CAGR is not computable: FY2026 EPS (-6.0c) sits on a weighted-average share count blended across the 40:1 consolidation and is not comparable to any prior year's EPS on a pre-consolidation basis. Owner FCF CAGR is not computable either -- FY2025 owner FCF was negative (-$8,525k after lease-principal and interest-income deductions) so no valid CAGR base exists between FY2025 and FY2026. None of the standard CAGR anchors are usable here; the DCF growth path is instead built bottom-up from FY2026 actuals, management's explicit FY2027 'no substantive market growth' guidance, and the $4m realised cost-out program, per the component-build method (section 2 of owner-fcf.md).

base.narrative: Base case: FY27 essentially flat (management's own 'no substantive market growth' guidance) as the $4m FY26 cost-out program delivers its full-year benefit and margin recovers from 8.76% (FY26, EBITDA before significant items) toward an 11% mid-cycle level -- well below the FY18/FY21 pre-oversupply peaks of 15-16.6%, reflecting the Commerce Commission's own finding that the NZ glass market remains structurally oversupplied. Modest volume recovery resumes from FY28 as NZ/AU building consents stabilise off trough and regulatory tailwinds (NZ Building Code, AU NatHERS) lift the double-glazing mix. Terminal value capped at 6x FCF (~4.9x FY26 EBITDA), the top of the stock's own 10-year trading range -- this is a chronically low-multiple name that has never re-rated above ~4.9x EV/EBITDA even at its best years, so the base case deliberately does not assume it starts now.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the failed Viridian takeover and persistent NZ oversupply keep consolidation optionality alive -- a rationalisation of processing capacity (by Metro or a competitor exiting) restores pricing power faster than base case assumes. AGG's import-model transition stabilises ahead of schedule and Australia's 1.2-million-new-homes target starts flowing into AGG volumes. Regulatory tailwinds (Building Code, NatHERS) drive faster mix-shift to higher-margin Low-E/laminated/frameless product. Margin reaches 13.5% (still below the FY18/21 peak of 15-16.6%, so not assuming a full return to the pre-oversupply structure) and the market begins to grant a modest re-rate (7x terminal cap vs 6x base, still below the stock's own historical ceiling of ~4.9x EV/EBITDA at the margin level, i.e. conservative even in the bull case).

bear.narrative: Bear case: the construction downturn deepens rather than stabilises -- NZ consent momentum (already slowing mid-2026, architects forecasting a pipeline contraction) turns into a further multi-year decline, and Victoria/AU stays subdued longer than AGG's import-model cost base can absorb. Oversupply persists, pricing stays under pressure, and the FY26 cost-out program only partially offsets continued revenue erosion. Covenant headroom (renegotiated Sept-2025, expires Sept-2028) tightens again -- reflected in the highest WACC of the three scenarios (15.0%, a solvency-risk premium specific to this path, not a generic cyclicality charge) rather than a going-concern breach outright, since the FY26 recapitalisation genuinely reset the balance sheet (net debt $27.0m vs $60.5m FY25, three-year facility to Sept-2028). Terminal multiple capped at 5x FCF, below the stock's own historical trading floor.

no_re_rate_reference.description: Memo value only, per dcf-methods section 7 optional guidance for chronically low-multiple names. MPG.NZ has never traded above ~4.9x EV/EBITDA (or ~0.69x P/B) in its 10-year Yahoo price history (consolidation-adjusted). This applies the stock's own historical EV/EBITDA ceiling (4.9x) directly to year-10 base-case EBITDA rather than capitalizing FCF at a multiple, as a cross-check on the house terminal value.
no_re_rate_reference.note: The house base case (IV $2.50, implied EV/EBITDA 4.86x) already sits almost exactly at this ceiling, confirming the 6x-FCF terminal cap was calibrated correctly rather than assuming a re-rate. This reference value is presented as a sanity cross-check, not a fourth scenario.

sensitivity.note: Terminal-growth columns are flat because the 6x-FCF terminal cap binds at every combination in this range -- Gordon growth only exceeds the cap below a terminal growth rate of roughly -2.7%, which is outside any plausible scenario. This is the correct, honest result for a name whose terminal value is constrained by its own trading history rather than by the growth assumption: the sensitivity that matters here is WACC (which does vary the value materially, $2.13-$2.95) and the terminal cap multiple itself, not terminal growth. Flagged rather than manufactured variation to avoid a misleading grid.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight set above the 15% house default (to 20%) because the business is only ~11 months past a dilutive recapitalisation that removed going-concern doubt, and management itself flags 'enough uncertainty' to withhold FY27 numeric guidance -- the downside path (deepening construction downturn, renewed covenant stress) is more than a generic margin-compression case. Bull weight trimmed to 30% (from 35% default) because the bull case needs several distinct things to go right independently: NZ market rationalisation/consolidation (outside management's control, and the Commerce Commission has already shown skepticism of consolidation via its Viridian scrutiny), AU volume recovery timing, and margin execution beyond the already-actioned $4m cost-out. Base held at 50%, reflecting management's own conservative 'no substantive market growth' framing as the most probable path.

sanity_check.methodology: Step 8c: implied multiples vs 10-year trading history from Yahoo Finance monthly closes. MPG.NZ's price history requires a 40:1 consolidation adjustment for all months before 6-Mar-2026 (raw Yahoo closes of ~$0.04 in early 2026 are pre-consolidation; multiplying by 40 makes them comparable to the post-consolidation ~$0.90-1.15 seen from Feb-2026 onward). Market-cap/EV level was used for the comparison (shares-on-issue x raw price = shares-on-issue x price, invariant to which side the 40x adjustment is applied) to sidestep needing a fully reconstructed per-share series.
sanity_check.price_series_check: Yahoo monthly closes confirm the 40:1 break is real and priced correctly: 2026-01 $0.040 (pre-consolidation) jumps to 2026-02 $1.055 (post-consolidation, post rights-issue dilution) -- a ~26x move consistent with the 40:1 ratio partially offset by the ~5.3x dilution from the rights issue + Amari placement (185.4m pre-raise shares -> 983.6m post-raise pre-consolidation shares -> 24.6m post-consolidation shares). Current price $0.925 (2026-08-20) is a live, liquid, consolidation-adjusted regular-close print on NZX (NZE), not a stale quote.

historical_multiple_range.ev_ebitda_range: 2.78x (FY2021) to 4.90x (FY2019), excluding the FY2024 near-zero-EBITDA outlier ($-0.3m EBITDA, multiple not meaningful)

sanity_check.outcome: PASS with fix applied. Current EV/EBITDA (2.73x, on FY2026 EBITDA before significant items of $18.24m) sits at the low end of the 10-year historical range (2.78-4.90x), and current P/B (0.38x) sits mid-range (0.25-0.69x) -- both consistent with a real, liquid market price and NOT a stale-quote artefact. However, the FIRST DCF build (before the sanity check) used an 8x-FCF terminal cap that implied a base-case EV/EBITDA of 5.32x -- ABOVE the top of the stock's own 10-year trading ceiling (4.90x), i.e. silently assuming a re-rate this name has never earned. FIX APPLIED: terminal cap multiples were tightened across all three scenarios (base 8x->6x FCF, i.e. ~4.86x EV/EBITDA; bull 9x->7x; bear unchanged at effectively 5x) so the base case's implied exit multiple (4.86x EV/EBITDA) sits just inside, not above, the stock's own historical ceiling. This is recorded in valuation_philosophy below. The bull case (8.43x implied EV/EBITDA) does still assume a re-rate beyond history -- that is a deliberate, named bull-case assumption (market consolidation / Viridian-style precedent), not a modelling error, and the no_re_rate_reference block gives a memo cross-check against the house base case.

valuation_philosophy: This build applied a sanity fix after the Step 8c check: the initial base-case terminal cap (8x FCF) implied an EV/EBITDA exit multiple (5.32x) above MPG.NZ's own 10-year trading ceiling (4.90x) -- effectively assuming the market grants this stock a re-rating it has never earned in a decade of trading through multiple cycles, a takeover approach, and a near-death recapitalisation. The terminal cap was tightened to 6x FCF (base), 7x FCF (bull), 5x FCF (bear), producing base-case implied EV/EBITDA of 4.86x -- calibrated to sit at, not above, the historical ceiling. The resulting base-case intrinsic value ($2.50) still implies large upside (+171%) against the current $0.925 price; this is not a modelling artefact but reflects that the market is pricing MPG.NZ near the bottom of its own historical multiple range on FY2026 EBITDA that has already recovered materially off the FY2024 trough (EBITDA before significant items $18.2m FY26 vs -$0.3m FY24 reported / $16.9m FY25), with net debt cut from $60.5m to $27.0m and going-concern risk removed. The market appears to be pricing meaningful residual doubt about execution (new CEO/CFO, unproven covenant headroom, no FY27 numeric guidance) that the probability weights (20% bear / 50% base / 30% bull, bear above the house default) are intended to reflect in the flows rather than in an additional discount-rate penalty. A reader who believes the market's skepticism is structural rather than transitional should weight the bear case materially higher than this build does.
